meta.description: A reminder that keeps asking over Telegram until you tap an answer. Everything is configured in TWO places in one node: which agent asks, and the reminder list. Fork this workflow once per agent (Atomix for health, SPEDA for chores…), rename it, edit the list, activate. Asking and answering cost zero tokens — no LLM is involved unless you reply in words instead of tapping.

nodes.name: Every 5 minutes
nodes.notes:
This is the CLOCK, and it sets the finest resolution available to every reminder below. A reminder set for 08:30 fires on the first tick at or after 08:30, and `every_minutes` cannot be shorter than this interval.

Every 5 minutes is 288 ticks a day, each one HTTP + a database read. No tokens. Do not be tempted to slow it down to 'save' anything — there is nothing to save, and it would blunt every reminder's timing.

nodes.name: Reminder list
nodes.notes:
⚙️ EDIT HERE — the agent on one line, the reminders in one array. The comment block documents every field.

TO FORK FOR ANOTHER AGENT: duplicate the whole workflow (⋯ ▸ Duplicate), change AGENT, replace the reminder list, rename it something like 'Persistent reminders — Ultron', and activate. The two run side by side; nothing is shared but the code.

Safe to leave empty: no items means the run stops here, green, having done nothing.

nodes.name: Igor: reminder tick
nodes.notes:
Hands the whole list to Igor, which decides everything: which reminders are due, which open ones are ready to re-ask, and which have run out of asks. It sends each question over the chosen agent's Telegram bot with the answer buttons attached.

NO LLM RUNS HERE. Asking, re-asking, giving up and recording a tapped answer are all deterministic — that is what makes a 5-minute nag affordable.

Answering: tap a button and it closes instantly, still with no turn. Or just reply in words ('aldım') — that is a normal Telegram conversation with the agent, which costs one turn, and the agent closes the reminder with its `reminders` tool.

The response lists what was sent / gave_up / waiting; open it in an execution to see what happened. neverError keeps a backend blip from failing the run every 5 minutes.
